title: Pre-registration
text:
# Argon v2 pre-registration: can an AI trade?

Written and committed **before** the AI desk has any scored decisions. The commit that adds this file, and its
timestamp in the GitHub history, is the proof of when it was written. Nothing below may change after that commit;
any later change has to be a new, dated section at the bottom, and the original stays as it is.

## What is frozen (from 20 October 2026)

- **Strategies:** the main strategy (London session, settings re-picked monthly from the previous 6 months) and the
  opening-range breakout on the Nasdaq (settings re-picked monthly, 20-day trend filter allowed). No new strategies,
  settings or filters are added to these. New ideas go to the research scout's separate "explorer" track only.
- **Costs and fills:** limit orders fill only if price trades one full tick through; stops slip 1 tick (3 ticks in
  the first 15 minutes of the US session); real per-market costs on every trade; no trading on contract roll days,
  no new trades 8:25-8:40 New York, flat by 1:55pm on Fed decision days and 3:55pm on other days.
- **The AI desk:** four Claude prompts with separate jobs and separate memories (Scout, Sceptic, Risk on
  claude-haiku-5-5; Chief on claude-sonnet-5-5). The prompts in `engine/agents.py` at this commit are frozen. Each
  agent rewrites its own lessons every Friday; that is part of the design, declared here in advance.
- **Risk:** 0.5% of the paper account per trade.

## The question and the hypotheses

**Main question:** do the setups the AI desk chooses to take do better than simply taking every setup the rules find?

- **H1 (main):** the average result of setups the desk takes is higher than the average of all setups.
- **H2:** the desk's picks beat the rules-only trader over the same days.
- **H3:** the desk's picks beat Kronos-small's direction calls on the same setups.
- **H4:** the desk's picks beat buying and holding the Nasdaq over the same months.

## How it will be measured

- **Period:** 1 January 2027 to 31 March 2027, live, forward only (an AI can't be fairly tested on the past).
- **Unit:** every setup the rules flag is played out to its result whether the desk takes it or not.
- **Test for H1:** difference in average R (taken minus all), with a 95% confidence range from a **day-clustered
  bootstrap** (every setup from the same day, across all markets, is resampled together), 10,000 resamples.
- **Minimum sample:** no verdict unless **at least 100 desk decisions** are scored. Fewer than 100 by 31 March means
  the result is reported as **"inconclusive: not enough decisions"**, whatever the numbers look like.
- **Verdicts:** *yes* if the whole 95% range is above zero; *no* if the whole range is below zero; otherwise
  *can't tell*. Reported exactly like that, even if it's disappointing.
- **Also reported, not tested:** how often the four agents disagree (if almost never, they are effectively one
  opinion); the desk's results in R and in dollars on whole micro contracts; Sharpe, Sortino and worst drop.

## What the agents' explanations are worth

The desk is scored on its **decisions** only. The agents' written reasons and weekly lessons are recorded as text and
treated as ideas to test, not as evidence.


## Freeze record

- **Frozen at commit** `cdefedc2715294c25842c50fedc0548ce6cc4ae2` (20 October 2026). The rules, costs, prompts and model versions above are the ones in that commit. GitHub's history shows its timestamp and that nothing above this section has changed since.

## Amendment 1 (20 October 2026)

- The freeze is **lifted** at Dru's request, so changes can still be made. Every change from now is logged in the changelog.
- Before the AI experiment starts, the rules will be **frozen again** with a new freeze record here. The evaluation window (1 January to 31 March 2027), the tests and the N ≥ 100 rule above stay exactly as written.
- The forward test only counts from the date of the new freeze.

## Amendment 2 (27 October 2026)

- **Risk per trade is now 0.75%** of the account (was 0.5%). One constant: `RISK` in `site/src/app1.js` and `engine/stats.py`.
- **New portfolio planned** (replacing the old main strategy + opening range): QuantLab first-candle/EMA rule, noise band,
  ATR band (all Nasdaq NQ) and the options-expiry reversal (NQ + ES). It goes into the engine only after the
  100-adjustment test below.
- **Honest limit on what the backtest can prove.** The four base strategies *and their settings* were chosen after seeing
  the whole history, including 2025–2026. So the 2025–2026 lockbox in `research/` only tests the **adjustments**
  (netting, sizing, loss limits, exits and so on), not the base portfolio. The only clean test of the base portfolio is
  the live paper trading from 1 January 2027.
- **Adjustment test, rules fixed in advance:** the list is in `research/ADJUSTMENTS.md`, committed before any test ran
  (the commit time proves it). Tested on Jul 2021–Dec 2024 only. Pass bars: combo Sharpe +0.10 over the baseline, better
  than the baseline in at least 3 of the 4 years, still better at double costs, and nearby settings also better. Survivors
  are opened on 2025–2026 **once**. Fail = out, no retries.
- Data fix: September 2026 minutes were duplicated in one loader (two overlapping files). Fixed, see `research/README.md`.

## Amendment 3 (28 October 2026): the v2 book, fixed before going live

- **The book:** QuantLab (NQ, *skips FOMC days*, the one adjustment that survived the lockbox), noise band (NQ), ATR band (NQ),
  options-expiry reversal (NQ + ES). 1R per trade each, **0.75%** of the account per trade. Code: `engine/portfolio.py`,
  logic in `research/common.py` (the exact tested code).
- **No daily loss limit.** With exact trade timing every version made results worse (`research/results/SUMMARY.md`).
- **Kill switch:** creating `data/KILL` stops new trades and the site shows the book as stopped. Emergency use only.
- **Shadow strategy, pre-registered now:** the same book with 12-month risk-parity weights. It runs alongside on paper and
  **never** changes the main book. Judged only on live paper results: after 12 months it replaces the main weighting only if its
  live Sharpe is higher *and* its live worst drop is no worse.
- **Freeze:** these rules freeze at **31 Dec 2026 23:59 UTC**. After that, nothing about the book changes until the
  12-month review, apart from the kill switch.
- Full-history backtest (mostly in-sample, read the honesty notes): $100k → $740,805, Sharpe 1.19, worst drop −26.5%,
  2026 −6.0%. Out of sample (2025-01 to 2026-09) Sharpe ≈ 0.65.
- Still to do before 1 Jan: feed this book's live signals (from the daily tape) into the desk so the agents judge these setups
  instead of the old main strategy's.

### Amendment 3b (28 October 2026): round 2 + a second lockbox
- 17 adjustments and their nearby settings registered in `research/ADJUSTMENTS2.md` **before any round-2 test code exists**,
  after a 5-member council review. Tested on Jul 2021 - Sep 2026, then the survivors **and the base book** are opened once on
  a never-seen 2011-2020 lockbox (`data/lockbox2010/`, bought 28 Oct 2026, $26.17, checked on timestamps only).
- If the base book fails on 2011-2020, nothing changes: it still goes live on 1 Jan 2027 and the result is published.

### Amendment 3c (28 October 2026): roll-day bug fixed
- The engine's roll-day list was always **empty**: Databento switches contracts at 8pm New York, which belongs to the next
  session, and the engine only counted a switch between two sessions. So QuantLab and the ATR band never skipped roll days,
  despite the stated rule. Fixed in `research/common.py` (every contract switch marks its session).
- Effect on the v2 book (full history): Sharpe 1.19 → **1.16**, $100k → **$689k** (was $741k), worst drop −26.5% → −24.4%,
  double costs 1.01 → 0.98. 11 QuantLab and 9 ATR-band trades removed. The noise band has its own loader and was unaffected.
- This is a code fix to match an already-stated rule, not a tuning change. Round 1's lockbox verdict for Q24 was computed before
  the fix and is not re-run (one shot means one shot); round 2 uses the fixed code for both the baseline and every adjustment.

### Amendment 3d (28 October 2026): risk 1% per trade
- Risk per trade is now **1%** (was 0.75%), by Dru's choice, before the 31 Dec freeze. One constant: `RISK` in
  `site/src/app1.js` and `engine/stats.py`, `risk_pct` in `engine/portfolio.py`. Sharpe in R is unchanged; size of swings is not.
- Full history at 1% (with the roll-day fix): $100k → **$1.13M**, about +59% a year, worst drop **−32%**, 2026 −7.1%; double costs $680k.

### Amendment 3e (28 October 2026): QuantLab dropped, cost rule added
- After lockbox 2, 8 structural variations were compared on all eras (2011-17, 2018-20, 2021-26) with a selection rule
  committed **before** running (`research/variations.py`, results `research/results/VARIATIONS.md`): highest worst-era Sharpe,
  double-cost Sharpe at least the base's, ties to the simpler one. Picked **V5: drop QuantLab + skip any trade whose cost is over
  10% of 1R.** This is in-sample (every year has now been seen); the clean test is live from 1 Jan 2027.
- No variation made 2011-2017 profitable (best −0.54). The book is a bet that the post-2018 regime continues.
- New book, Jul 2021 - Sep 2026 at 1%: see data/portfolio.json. Risk-parity shadow continues on the new book.

### Amendment 3f (28 October 2026): keep QuantLab (Dru's choice, V4)
- Dru chose **V4: all four strategies + the 10%-of-1R cost rule** over the selection rule's pick V5 (drop QuantLab), after
  seeing both. Logged openly as a hindsight choice: V4 made more in both eras (2011-20: $92.7k vs $74.6k from $100k; 2021-26:
  $1.19M vs $282k at 1%) but with bigger drops (−70%/−32% vs −65%/−24%). QuantLab's gains are concentrated in a few big-news
  months (2024: +61R of its +77R came in July and November).
- The desk page (docs/desk.html) is embedded in the site as a preview with sample data.

## Amendment 4 (28 October 2026): the desk becomes a morning day-type forecaster (shadow test)
Designed after a 6-member council review (statistician, risk manager, trader, AI engineer, sceptic, methodologist).
- **Job:** every weekday 8:45-9:25am New York, before the open, forecast whether today is a TREND day or a CHOP day and pick a
  size for the whole v2 book: 0.5x / 1x / 1.5x. It never picks direction. Inputs are only things known before 9:30: overnight
  move and range, yesterday's range vs its 20-day average, 5-day RSI (dealer-gamma clue), VIX and its 1-year percentile,
  calendar (FOMC, options expiry, jobs Friday) and market headlines. Code: `engine/daytype.py`.
- **Three arms, all on paper from 1 Jan 2027, none changes the real book:** (1) 1x, (2) dumb rule: yesterday's range / 20-day
  average > 1.2 -> 1.5x, < 0.8 -> 0.5x, else 1x, (3) AI forecast. A day never risks more than 4R in total (size x trades <= 4).
- **AI rules:** model pinned to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, temperature 0, asked 3 times, MEDIAN size used; prompt frozen, fingerprint
  `8b27b11cc4cadeba`; it reads no self-written lessons. Veto only for: breaking_unscheduled_event, market_halt, data_feed_broken, and only if
  2 of 3 runs agree. Not finished by 9:25 -> counts as 1x (logged as late).
- **Scoring:** `engine/daytype_score.py`: Sharpe of each arm (monthly R), plus the Brier score of the AI's trend probability
  against whether the book made money before costs that day.
- **Promotion rule:** after **at least 120 scored trading days**, the AI arm takes real control only if its Sharpe beats
  **both** other arms by **at least +0.15**. Otherwise it stays shadow and the result is published either way.
- **Any change to the model, prompt, inputs or rules restarts the 120-day clock.**
- The separate per-setup desk (Scout / Sceptic / Risk / Chief judging the original strategy's setups) continues as its own
  experiment, scored against "take every setup". It does not touch the v2 book.

### Amendment 4b (2 November 2026): an objective trend label, and the AI council (exploratory)
- **Trend day, fixed now:** |close − open| ≥ 0.6 × (high − low) for NQ's 9:30–16:00 session. This is the label the morning
  forecasts are scored against (Brier score and accuracy). The book's own result is recorded separately as the trading outcome,
  because scoring a forecast with the strategy it sizes would be circular. No forecasts had been scored yet, so nothing is lost.
- **The AI council** (a separate, exploratory shadow test; it never touches the book or the main arms): every morning the same
  frozen prompt and the same inputs, at the same moment, go to Claude (the existing forecaster) and to other model families:
  Gemini (Google), Llama (via Groq) and optionally GPT (via OpenRouter). Temperature 0, each asked once, raw answers and timestamps
  saved. Model ids are pinned in `engine/daytype.py`; any change restarts the council's clock. All ids must be confirmed and
  pinned before the 31 Dec freeze.
- **Combining rule, fixed now:** council trend probability = the average of the members' probabilities; council size = the
  median of their sizes (with an even number, the average of the two middle ones). Sizes are all on the 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 scale.
- **Missing answers, fixed now:** a member with no key, an error or a late answer counts as no answer that day. A session counts
  only if at least 3 members answered. No session is dropped for any other reason.
- **Measured:** each member's accuracy and Brier score, the council's, how often two members are wrong on the same day compared
  with what independence would predict (do they make different mistakes?), and the council's trading result. Judged only after
  at least **250 counted sessions**.

### Amendment 5 (3 November 2026): the per-setup desk is retired
- The four-agent desk that judged the original strategy's setups is switched off and its code moved to `engine/retired/`,
  unchanged. It never judged a setup (see `engine/retired/README.md`). The AI's role in Argon v2 is now the morning call and the
  council (Amendments 4 and 4b). The 3D desk becomes the window onto those, the book's live view and the official ledger.

### Amendment 6 (2 November 2026): the live paper book
- **The official record is the nightly ledger**, `engine/live.py`, built to the council review in `research/COUNCIL_LIVE.md`
  (committed before the code). It runs the exact backtest code (`engine/portfolio.py` → `research/common.py`) every night on that
  day's Databento 1-minute data. There is no separate live version of any strategy.
- **Money:** $100,000 on 1 Jan 2027. Micro contracts (MNQ $2/pt, MES $5/pt), rounded DOWN to whole contracts at 1% of the
  account, capped at 200 per trade; the account compounds in dollars day by day (every trade sized from that morning's account).
  A trade too wide for one micro is logged as skipped. Costs: the research costs in points (official); a double-cost ledger runs alongside.
- **Ledger:** append-only, one entry per session, trade id `strategy|symbol|date|entry minute|variant`, each entry hashed and
  linked to the previous one, with the code commit and each market's last bar recorded. Published daily in `data/ledger/`.
- **Every run, in order:** kill switch; chain check; **replay check** (every booked day is rebuilt with today's code and data and
  must match exactly, else the book halts and alerts; the ledger is never rewritten); data gate (a session is booked only when all
  four markets' data reaches past 16:00 New York); book every missed session; position check (flat after the close, else halt).
- **"Consistent with the backtest", fixed now:** `research/results/live_band.json`, sha256
  `9f5992a96a67a4e7aa6e3a2deef81697af455f8148b16e6169b09a71102c03e4`. After k finished live months (k = 1..12), the live rule-R so
  far (every trade the rules took, including ones too small for a micro) is compared with the 5th–95th percentile of the
  backtest's rolling k-month sums (Jul 2021 – Sep 2026). It is a flag, never a stop rule, and it is optimistic (mostly in-sample).
- **Unofficial live view:** the same code on Yahoo intraday bars, every 5 minutes in the desk loop. Always labelled unofficial.
- **Practice book** from 16 Nov 2026 in `data/ledger_practice/`, same code, so bugs show up before 1 Jan.
- Small code change with no effect on results: each trade now also records its entry price (stop and exit follow from it).

### Amendment 7 (7 November 2026, practice run, before any freeze): morning-call fixes
- **Bug fixed:** every morning call so far returned "no forecast". Claude 5.5 models reject the `temperature` setting (HTTP 400),
  and the council had no API keys. Those days count as 1x and stay in the practice record as they are.
- **No sampling settings for any AI** (models that reject them can't be compared fairly otherwise). Thinking is set by one shared
  **effort level** for every AI instead (`high` during practice).
- **Council:** Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek V4 Pro (replacing Llama, which Groq made enterprise-only), all through
  OpenRouter with the same prompt and inputs. DeepSeek avoids its own China-hosted API where another host serves the model.
  **Solo AI:** Claude Opus 5.5. Every failure's error message is now saved in the record.
- **Still to fix before the freeze (a later amendment):** the rule for which model each company races with ("top generally
  available model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index on the freeze date"), the final effort level, and the new freeze date.

### Amendment 8 (9 November 2026, before the freeze): a stronger morning call
- **Sizes:** 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x or **2x**. The one-line rule gains a 2x tier (yesterday's range above 1.6x its 20-day average).
  A day never risks more than **6%** in total (size x trades <= 6), for every competitor.
- **Memory:** each AI sees a short track record of its OWN past calls (hit rate, Brier score, average size, what its sizing added,
  and its last 20 calls with outcomes). It never sees Argon's notes or other AIs' records. The solo AI's three repeat calls use
  prompt caching (same text, lower cost).
- **Two-round council:** round 1 = each member answers alone and privately (scored as "council R1"). Round 2 = each member sees
  the others' round-1 answers, anonymous and in a random order fixed by the date, then gives a final private answer (scored as
  "council R2"). Comparing R1 with R2 tests whether discussion helps or just causes herding.
- **Random sizer:** a 'luck' competitor whose size each day comes from sha256("argon-random-sizer-v1|date"). If the AIs can't
  beat it, they show no skill.
- **News:** headlines published since the previous trading day's 4pm close, from Yahoo Finance and MarketWatch. The AIs are told
  headlines are untrusted data; headlines that look like instructions are kept out and logged.
- **Fair limits:** every AI gets the same effort level, the same time limit and one retry; failures are saved with their error.
- **Brain:** every booked day gets a note (trades, every AI's call, headlines, analysis), plus monthly pages and a Decisions page.
  The ledger stays the official record.
- Practice changes only: nothing here touches a booked result. Still to fix before the freeze: the final models, effort level and
  freeze date (31 Jan 2027).

### Amendment 9 (9 November 2026, before the freeze): statistics plan, market forecaster, integrity
- **Dates:** official ledger and Race 1 start **1 February 2027**; rules freeze **31 January 2027, 23:59 UTC**.
- **Statistics plan, fixed now:** `research/results/stats_plan.json` (sha256 `d37d866301ab5a60c8fa52e1b3c7eb03d95127313a4f65156f65b5b32e024a5e`). Paired circular block bootstrap of the
  annualised Sharpe difference on daily returns (blocks of 5 days), one-sided, Holm-corrected at 5% across: AI vs 1x, AI vs the
  one-line rule, council round 2 vs solo AI. **Pass** = AI beats 1x AND the one-line rule after Holm, in Race 1 and again in Race 2.
  A gap under +0.30 annualised Sharpe is reported but not called meaningful.
- **Checked on fake data before any race data exists:** with no real skill the test wrongly declares a winner 0.5% of the time.
  **Power is low:** with ~230 days it only reliably detects very large edges (around +1.2 to +1.3 Sharpe for ~70-80% power).
  So a "no" in Race 1 can mean "too small to see", which is one reason for Race 2.
- **Market forecaster** (`research/results/market_forecaster.json`, sha256 `81f1382cc120bf743f4f5d3171fd8a67a75562f23fd86be802627bfd9d097a0c`): a frozen logistic regression on the VIX's
  1-year percentile and yesterday's range ratio, fitted once on Jul 2021-Sep 2026, with fixed size cut-offs. In-sample it barely
  beats guessing (Brier 0.2363 vs 0.2365), so it is the "what the market data already says" benchmark. Scored as a shadow arm.
- **Missed calls:** a day with no AI call (late or failed) is MISSING and left out of every comparison; never filled in as 1x.
- **Accounts:** each competitor gets its own compounding paper account and worst-drawdown figure.
- **Integrity:** the ledger's head hash is stamped nightly with OpenTimestamps (anchored in Bitcoin), so its history can't be
  rewritten even by force-pushing; Databento closes are cross-checked against Yahoo nightly (over 1% gap, outside roll days, alerts).
- **Cost:** each call's tokens and dollars are recorded; a day over $3 alerts the phone.

### Amendment 10 (19 November 2026, before the freeze): main book and size, decided by Dru
- **Main book:** G3 trade filter (analysis/BATCH24) on the package: VXN-managed Nasdaq core at 1x plus the four rules.
- **Size: rules weight 0.625**, i.e. **0.625% of the account at risk per rules trade** (up from 0.5%). G3 only ever skips;
  it never sizes a trade up. Chosen by Dru after batch 30 showed no core/rules mix beats G3 without more risk.
- **Backtest at this size (single run, not blind, ~296 trials):** 2021–26 +71.5% a year / Sortino 3.72 / worst drop
  −20.5% / crash chance 0.7%; 2010–20 +31.0% / 2.39 / −23.8% / 3.1%; 2026 to 12 Nov +29.9%, worst drop −20.5%.
  Batch 29's jitter test showed G3's single-run figures carry about ±3 points (2021–26) and ±1.5 (2010–20) of luck,
  so these are upper-middle estimates, not promises. Plan for worse drops live.
- **Accepted trade-off:** about 2 to 2.5 points deeper worst drop than at 0.5%, still inside the "never riskier than the
  Nasdaq alone" limit in both eras.
- **Shadows (paper only, never change the main book):** G3 at 0.5%; skip-only at 0.625%.
- Recorded now; becomes binding with the freeze record (31 January 2027). The live engine's sizing is changed to match
  as part of wiring G3 into it, and that change is logged in the freeze record.

### Amendment 11 (19 November 2026, before the freeze): how the desk's models are chosen, decided by Dru
- **Rule:** the desk's AIs are the best models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (artificialanalysis.ai),
  taken from ONE snapshot of that page saved before the freeze (planned 24 January 2027):
  - seat 1: the top Anthropic model; seat 2: the top OpenAI model; seat 3: the top Google model;
  - seat 4: the top model with a public API from **any other developer** (replaces the DeepSeek seat, whose best
    model scored far below the rest).
- Each at the reasoning setting it was ranked at; exact model IDs and settings written into the freeze record.
- **Pinned for all of Race 1.** Newer models released during the race are logged, not swapped in (Race 2 may update).
- **Reading today (19 Nov 2026, for reference only, not binding):** Claude Fable 5.2 (max) 65, GPT-6.2 Astra (max) 62,
  Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh) 61, Kimi K3.1 Pro 46 (Meta's Muse Wonder Full scores 50 but has no public API).
- What it measures: the best general-purpose AI per seat, not the best trading AI; nobody ranks trading skill, which
  is what Race 1 tests.
- **Speed fallback (same for every seat):** if a seat's top model fails to answer before the 09:25 cutoff on more than
  10% of practice mornings in January 2027, that seat uses the same developer's next-best model on the snapshot.
  Decided now, before anyone knows which seat (if any) it will affect.

### Amendment 12 (19 November 2026, practice only, before the freeze): council vs memory, decided later
- Dru's decision: during the practice run, test BOTH (A) the four-model council (Amendment 11 seats, one call each,
  median, no debate round) and (B) a memory arm (the same AI plus a short daily digest of the brain's live notes).
- One of them becomes the official AI arm in the freeze record, chosen before the freeze; the choice will be made on
  reliability, speed and cost in practice, NOT on practice-run performance (too few days to mean anything).
- The no-news arm is dropped.

### Amendment 13 (20 November 2026, before the freeze): after the multiple-testing check (batch 34)
Why: batch 34 (`analysis/BATCH34_RESULTS.md`, rules committed before the run) found that G3's gain over the plain
package is not proven once ~299 trials are counted (pooled t 2.20 vs a bar of 3.09-3.59; in 2021-26 t 0.55), and that
the desk's promotion rule would promote an AI with no skill about one time in five. Reviewed with Gemini.
Main-book choice made by Claude at Dru's request ("up to you, as long as it's profitable").

**Main book (replaces Amendment 10's choice)**
- **Main book: the plain package at 0.5%**: VXN-managed Nasdaq core at 1x plus the four rules taking every signal, 0.5% of
  the account at risk per rules trade. Backtest (single run, in-sample, not blind): 2021-26 +56.4% a year, Sortino 3.18,
  worst drop -19.4%; 2010-20 +21.6%, 1.75, -23.5%. Expect live results well below these.
- **Why not G3:** its gain is about zero in the recent era, its better 2010-20 figures were part of why it was picked, and
  it adds a monthly model and 24 daily inputs that are not yet live. When the complex version cannot prove it beats the
  simple one, the simple one is the default. Not chosen by looking at any new result for the package itself.
- **Shadow (paper only):** G3 at 0.5% (replaces both Amendment 10 shadows). Its live replay must match its backtest
  decisions trade for trade by **10 January 2027**, or it is logged as "not counted" for Race 1.
- **Size is final at 0.5%.** The 0.625% option is closed.
- Statement for every write-up: *"G3's gain over the package was not significant after correcting for ~299 tests;
  Race 1 runs both side by side to measure it live."*
- **No re-weighting and no dropping rules.** The before/after-May-2024 differences are noise (no rule's change has |t| > 1).
  Watch item: at the end of Race 1, re-run the same table (now ~3.5 years after May 2024) and flag any rule whose
  cumulative expectancy since May 2024 is at or below 0R for review in Race 2. Expiry is noted separately (daily options
  may be eroding the monthly expiry effect).
- Trial count: "~299" is every trial listed across the batch documents; 185 is the number with saved results in both eras
  (identical results counted once). The rest were single-era, side-market or rerun tests. None are hidden.

- **Live engine, from the 23 November 2026 session (practice book):** rules trades at 0.5%, plus the Nasdaq core
  (`engine/core.py`): micro Nasdaq futures held from the previous close to this close, `w` = min(1.5, one-year median of
  VXN / latest VXN), rounded to the **nearest** whole contract (rounding down would hold about half the target on $100k);
  the pre-FOMC leg (previous close to 13:59 on decision days, with costs); T-bill interest (FRED DTB3). Each day's core
  inputs are saved when the day is first booked, so replays are exact. Days booked before the switch replay unchanged.
  Known gap: with whole contracts the core can only approximate `w` (one MNQ is about half of a $100k account).

**The desk's test (replaces Amendment 4's promotion rule)**
- **Headline = every trading day** (intention to treat). A morning with fewer than 3 valid seats, no headlines on a normal
  weekday, or a quote older than 5 minutes is "degraded", decided only by checks logged before 09:25; it counts at 1x and
  with a trend chance equal to the 2021-26 base rate of trend days. No day is ever dropped or reclassified afterwards.
  Full-input days are reported only as a side note.
- **Primary scientific test, two steps, one-sided 5%, stationary block bootstrap (10,000 draws, average block 5 days):**
  1. The council's trend chance ranks trend days above chop days: AUC against the fixed trend-day label > 0.50.
     If this fails, no forecasting skill is claimed and nothing further is tested.
  2. Only if step 1 passes: its AUC beats the frozen market-data forecaster's (Amendment 9) on the same days.
  Brier skill and calibration are reported as secondary diagnostics, not pass marks.
- **Promotion to real control (Race 2 at the earliest):** both steps pass AND the council's result beats 95% of 10,000
  reshuffles of its own daily sizes (same average size, so betting bigger earns nothing).
- **Stated in advance:** about 230 days can detect a clear skill (AUC ~0.58: ~88% chance) but not a small one (AUC ~0.54:
  ~37%). A "no skill shown" result does not prove the AI has none.
- Checked first: the trend-day label lines up with the rules' profit (trend days +0.65% vs chop -0.20% a day in 2021-26,
  t ~10; same in 2010-20), so forecasting trend days is the right target. Label window fixed: NQ 09:30-16:00 New York;
  half days are not traded and not scored.

**Desk inputs and models**
- **No track record in the council's prompt.** Amendment 8's "own past calls and last 20 outcomes" is removed (what is shown
  in a prompt steers the model). If Amendment 12's memory arm (B) is chosen instead, it may show only a neutral block
  (days logged, trend-day rate, its average trend chance, its size mix), shows "not enough data" until 30 live days exist,
  and contains no lessons, streaks or recent trades.
- **Model snapshot moves to 2-4 January 2027** (from 24 January), so the four race models run all of January's practice and
  the speed fallback can be judged on them.
- Frozen with each model: exact model id, provider (OpenRouter host fixed, no silent fallback to another host),
  temperature, reasoning effort and max tokens. One call per seat in Race 1. In January practice each seat is asked twice
  to measure how often its answer flips (a diagnostic only).
- **08:45 cutoff:** if the call runs late, it still only sees data up to 08:45; headlines are time-stamped and any published
  after 08:45 are dropped.
- Logged every day, no pass marks: whether each seat answered, whether news loaded, the cost of the call, and whether the
  council's size moves with VIX.

**Integrity**
- At the freeze, the SHA-256 of this file and of every engine file is written to `FROZEN.txt`.
- Planned (separate pre-registration before any data is bought): one frozen, no-changes run of the four rules on Russell
  2000 futures (RTY, CME data 2018-2026), rules only, no Nasdaq core.


### Amendment 14 (21 November 2026, before the freeze): a second news source for the morning call
- Headlines now come from the Yahoo Finance and MarketWatch RSS feeds **plus Finnhub's general market news** (free tier, key in
  the `FINNHUB_API_KEY` secret). Each Finnhub story keeps its own outlet's name, e.g. "Reuters (Finnhub)".
- Same rules as before: only stories published after the previous 4pm close and before the call, at most 12, duplicates
  dropped, possible prompt-injection lines kept out and logged. The sources take turns so one outlet can't fill every slot.
- If Finnhub fails or has no key, the call runs on the RSS feeds alone; "news loaded" is logged per source.
- Frozen with the rest of the desk inputs on 31 January 2027.

### Amendment 15 (21 November 2026, before the freeze): Argon-1, our own trained forecaster (shadow seat; test 3 starts early)
- **Question:** can a small model trained only for this job, at no cost, match the frontier AIs at the 08:45 trend-day call?
  This is "test 3" (an LLM vs a machine-learning model), run inside Race 1 so both are scored on the same days.
- **Same target and scoring as the AI seats:** trend day = |close - open| >= 0.6 x (high - low), NQ 09:30-16:00; scored with
  the Amendment 13 two-step test and the Amendment 9 bootstrap. **Shadow only:** it never sizes a real trade in Race 1.
- **Inputs (all before 08:45 New York):** the last 256 five-minute bars of NQ and ES, plus daily inputs (overnight moves,
  yesterday's range and shape, RSI 5, VIX close and its 1-year percentile, Fed day, options expiry, jobs Friday, weekday).
  **No headlines**, so the comparison is "price data only" vs "AI that also reads the news". NQ and ES only, because the
  2011-2020 data has nothing else.
- **Two candidates, one chosen by a rule fixed now:** (A) Kronos-small kept frozen (pinned weights and code), its summary of
  the bars squeezed to 32 numbers per market (fitted on training days only), plus a regularised logistic regression;
  (B) a tiny transformer trained from scratch. Baseline: a logistic regression on VIX percentile and range ratio.
- **Data split:** train Jan 2011 - Dec 2020; choose on Jan 2021 - Dec 2023 (lower log-loss of A and B, and it must beat the
  baseline, otherwise it is chosen anyway and flagged as failing validation); **test once** on Jan 2024 - Oct 2026 (the code
  refuses to open it twice; reported whatever it says, never used to change anything); then refit the choice on
  Jan 2011 - Oct 2026 with the same settings and freeze it (sha256 of the weights in `research/results/argon1_frozen.json`
  and `FROZEN.txt`). Note: the 2011-2020 data was opened in Amendment 3b and used since, so no backtest number here is
  out-of-sample. Only Race 1's forward days are a real test.
- **Size:** the market forecaster's rule (cut-offs at the 25th, 65th and 85th percentiles of the model's own in-sample
  chances): 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x or 2x.
- **Live:** runs in the 08:45 desk job (no API cost) on Yahoo's delayed 5-minute bars; checks the weights' fingerprint
  before every call; a day with no call is MISSING, as for the AIs. Known gap: Yahoo's continuous contract does not mark
  roll nights, so those mornings are flagged `roll_risk` and reported separately.
- **After Race 1:** the same pipeline can be rerun with a later end date ("Argon-2") for test 3 proper, frozen again before
  its own race. Argon-1 itself is never retrained during Race 1.
- Code: `research/argon1/` (plan in `research/ARGON1_PLAN.md`), training workflow `.github/workflows/argon1.yml`.

### Amendment 16 (23 November 2026, before the freeze): the morning call can skip the day
- The AI seats (and the council) may now answer size **0 = skip**: the whole book sits the day out. The menu is
  0 / 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2. The prompt says skipping also skips the winning days, so 0 is for days the AI judges clearly worse
  than normal. The restricted VETO (breaking unscheduled event, market halt, broken data) stays as it was.
- The random sizer ("luck" arm) draws from the same five sizes, so it can skip too, keeping the comparison fair.
- Scoring is unchanged: a skipped day scores 0R for that arm. The comparisons that matter are against the one-line rule,
  the random sizer and a constant size matched to the arm's own average size (to be added before the freeze).
- Why: 23 Nov 2026 (no call that day) was a whipsaw after huge news, the kind of day a skip could help on. Whether the
  AIs skip the right days is part of what Race 1 tests; one anecdote is not evidence.

109 adjustments, written down **before any test ran** (this commit's timestamp is the proof). Generated from `research/adjustments.py`; `research/run_all.py` tests exactly these.

## Rules (fixed in advance)

- **Baseline:** QuantLab (walk-forward, 6 variants) + noise band (walk-forward, 8 variants) + ATR band + expiry (NQ+ES), each 1R per trade, summed.
- **Test window:** Jul 2021 to Dec 2024 (42 months). 2025-01 onward is the **lockbox**, not simulated at all.
- **Same realism as always:** costs NQ 0.75 / ES 0.5 pts, stop slippage, roll days skipped, flat 3:55 (1:55 on FOMC days), monthly re-pick from the previous 6 months.
- **Pass bars** (all must hold): combo Sharpe at least **+0.10** over baseline (raised from +0.05 because of ~100 trials); better than baseline in at least **3 of the 4 years** (2021 H2, 2022, 2023, 2024); still at least **+0.05** better at **double costs**; every **nearby setting** at least +0.05 better.
- **Risk levels (S)** can't change a Sharpe measured in R, so they are reported (yearly return, worst drop, halving chance), not passed or failed.
- **Lockbox:** Survivors are run ONCE on 2025-01..2026-09. Pass = Sharpe above the baseline at normal AND double costs. Fail = out.
- **Honesty note:** the 4 base strategies and their settings were chosen after seeing 2025-2026, so the lockbox only tests these adjustments. The only clean test of the base portfolio is live from 1 Jan 2027.

# Lockbox (opened once, 2026-10-28)

The single survivor of the 109 pre-registered adjustments was run once on the locked months, Jan 2025 to Sep 2026.

| | Sharpe | R | 2025 | 2026 (to Sep) | Sharpe, double costs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (4 strategies) | 0.52 | +52.5R | +57.1R | −4.5R | 0.45 |
| **Q24: QuantLab skips FOMC days** | **0.65** | **+64.8R** | +63.4R | +1.4R | **0.59** |

**Verdict: KEEP.** It beat the baseline at normal and double costs, as pre-registered.

## Honest notes
- 1 of 109 passing is about what luck alone could produce, so the lockbox pass matters more than the test-window gain. It's still only 21 months.
- The baseline itself fell from Sharpe 1.41 (2021–2024) to 0.52 (2025–2026). The edges are decaying or 2026 is unusually choppy. Expect long flat stretches live.
- Exact-time daily loss limits all **hurt** (−2R: −0.11 Sharpe). The earlier +0.09 from the daily-total simulation came from its lookahead. Dropped.
- Risk parity (P13) raised Sharpe by +0.26 but failed the "better R in most years" bar, because it moves weight to the low-volatility legs and makes less R. That bar compares R, not risk-adjusted R, which is a flaw in my rule. It was not rescued: changing the rules after seeing results is exactly what the lockbox exists to stop. Any retest would need a fresh pre-registration and new data (live).
- A crash-check during setup printed results for 15 adjustments before the full run. The list was already committed, so nothing could change, but it is disclosed here.
- The 4 base strategies were chosen after seeing 2025–2026, so this lockbox only tests the adjustment. The clean test of the portfolio is live from 1 Jan 2027.

title: Round 2: the 17 adjustments
text:
# Argon v2: round 2 pre-registered adjustments + the 2010-2020 lockbox

17 adjustments, committed **before any round-2 test code exists**. Reviewed by a 5-member council (statistician, risk manager, execution trader, sceptic, methodologist).

**Baseline:** The final v2 book (Amendment 3): QuantLab (NQ, walk-forward, skips FOMC days) + noise band (NQ) + ATR band (NQ) + expiry reversal (NQ + ES), 1R per trade each, 0.75% risk, no daily loss limit.

## Rules (fixed now)

- Test window: Jul 2021 - Sep 2026. Lockbox: Jan 2011 - Dec 2020, opened ONCE, for the survivors AND the base book (B0), in a single run whose results are written to a file before anyone reads them.
- Pass marks (all must hold): Sharpe at least +0.10 over the baseline; better than the baseline in at least 4 of the 6 years, with each year compared at the SAME volatility (the adjustment's monthly series is rescaled to the baseline's standard deviation first: this fixes round 1's risk-parity flaw); at least +0.05 better at double costs; every nearby setting at least +0.05 better.
- Lockbox pass: Sharpe at least +0.03 over the baseline at normal costs AND better at double costs. Fail = out, no retries.
- B0 (the base book itself on 2011-2020): passes if Sharpe >= 0.4, Sharpe > 0 at double costs, and positive in at least 6 of 10 years. IF B0 FAILS, NOTHING CHANGES: the book still goes live on 1 Jan 2027 and the write-up says so.
- Costs are real tick-based costs (NQ 0.75, ES 0.5 points a round trip, same slippage rules). NQ was ~2,000 in 2010 vs ~20,000 now, so costs in R were 5-10x heavier then. Results at real costs are what count; a version with costs scaled to the price level is reported for information only and cannot rescue a fail.
- Data rule (both windows): skip any day missing more than 10% of its 9:30-16:00 minutes (checked on timestamps only: removes 0 lockbox days); half days (<=300 session minutes) are skipped by the loader as always (78 in the lockbox).
- FOMC days 2010-2020 from research/calendar_hist.py (Fed historical pages). Before Mar 2013 be flat by 12:25pm; 3 Mar 2020 by 9:55am; otherwise 1:55pm.
- Walk-forward strategies in the lockbox re-pick only from earlier lockbox months (warm-up Jun-Dec 2010), never from 2021+.
- Holiday = a weekday with no session or a session of <=300 minutes (derived from the data; holidays are known in advance in real life).
- Every "nearby" setting below is fixed now. Trials this round: 17 adjustments + 32 nearby settings, each also at double costs.

## Adjustments

|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | Risk parity: weight = 1/stdev of each strategy's last 12 months, average weight 1 | `{'rule': 'parity', 'look': 12}` | {'look': 9}; {'look': 15} |  |

| R04 | Volatility target for the whole book | `{'rule': 'voltarget', 'look': 6, 'cap': 1.5, 'floor': 0.5}` | {'look': 3, 'cap': 1.5, 'floor': 0.5}; {'look': 12, 'cap': 1.5, 'floor': 0.5} | scale = (expanding median of past monthly stdev, min 12 months) / (stdev of last `look` months), capped at 1.5x and floored at 0.5x |

| S01 | Add the noise band on ES (walk-forward, same variants) | `{'strat': 'noiseband', 'sym': 'ES', 'w': 1.0}` | {'w': 0.75}; {'w': 1.25} |  |

| X01 | QuantLab enters with a limit at the 9:35 open | `{'strat': 'quantlab', 'limit_ticks': 0}` | {'limit_ticks': -1}; {'limit_ticks': 1} | fills only if the 9:35 minute trades 1 full tick through the limit; otherwise market at the 9:36 open + 2 ticks. Worst case assumed inside the minute. |

| W03 | Re-pick looks back 12 months; if the best variant did not break even, use the default | `{'strat': 'both', 'look': 12, 'fallback': True}` | {'look': 9, 'fallback': True}; {'look': 15, 'fallback': True} | defaults: QuantLab candle stop + EMA exit; noise band 30 min, 1.0x band, VWAP stop |

## Dropped after review

- Early-close days (already skipped by the loader)
- QuantLab half size on big-gap days (near-copy of a round-1 failure)
- Daily loss limits, pullback/delayed entries, QuantLab filters, other markets (failed in round 1 or ruled out)

## Pre-commit checks (timestamps and counts only, no prices)

- Lockbox: 22 files, 2010-06-07 to 2020-12-31, sha256 in data/lockbox2010/MANIFEST.json, no duplicate minutes, symbol correct.
- 2,711 sessions per market; 0 days fail the 10% rule; 78 half days; first bar 9:30 New York on every session (DST correct); 4 rolls a year.
- 48 full-closure weekday holidays found (incl. Hurricane Sandy, 29 Oct 2012).
- FOMC: the engine calendar only covered 2021+, which would have silently broken the FOMC rules in the lockbox. Fixed: 88 decision days in research/calendar_hist.py.
- Nothing outside a lockbox run reads data/lockbox2010/.

title: Lockbox 2 (2011-2020)
text:
# Lockbox 2 (2011-2020, never seen before), opened once on 28 Oct 2026

## The base book (B0): **FAIL**
| | Sharpe | R | Sharpe, double costs | Positive years |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2 book, 2011-2020 | **−1.03** | **−469R** | −2.01 | 3 of 10 (2018, 2019, 2020) |
| same, costs scaled to price level (information only) | −0.30 | −128R | | |

By strategy (net of costs): QuantLab **−446R** (−62R even before costs; costs were 0.16R a trade because NQ was ~2,000-4,000),
noise band −18R (gross +40R), ATR band −8R (gross +29R), expiry +2R (gross +16R).

**What it means:** the opening-candle momentum edge (QuantLab) did not exist in 2011-2017, even before costs. The other three
had small edges that costs ate. Everything only works from about 2018, when Nasdaq volatility, price level and options and
leveraged-ETF flows changed. So either these edges are a recent market feature, or they were partly fitted to 2021-2026. The
backtest profit on 2021-2026 is very likely an overstatement of what to expect.

**As pre-registered, nothing changes because of this:** the book still goes live on 1 Jan 2027 and this result is published.

## Survivors from round 2
| | 2011-2020 Sharpe | vs base | double costs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 risk parity, 12 months | −0.82 | +0.21 | −1.56 (base −2.01) | **KEEP** |
| R03 risk parity, capped 0.5-2 | −0.93 | +0.10 | −1.80 | **KEEP** |

Both pass the pre-registered rule (better than the base at normal and double costs), but only because they shrink
QuantLab, the strategy that failed. They are less bad, not good. R01 was better in both windows.

## Disclosures
- A crash-check before the full run showed pass/fail for 10 of the 17 adjustments (all fail). The list was already committed.
- Two code bugs were found and fixed before this run (FOMC calendar missing 2010-2020; roll days never skipped). Both are in PREREGISTRATION.md.

text:
# research/

Rebuilt, saved copies of every test so a sandbox reset can't lose them again.

- `orig_qb.py`, `orig_deep.py`: the original QuantLab and deep-dive (noise band = part B) scripts, unchanged apart from ROOT, output paths and one data fix (below).
- `common.py`: the 4 portfolio strategies rebuilt with trade-level output + walk-forward + scoring helpers.
- `strat_quantlab.py`, `strat_noiseband.py`, `strat_atrband.py`, `strat_expiry.py` write `results/trades_*.csv` (date, entry time, exit time, side, R).

## Reproduction check (full history, `ARGON_FULL=1`)
| strategy | expected | rebuilt |
|---|---|---|
| QuantLab NQ (walk-forward) | 1,355 trades, +176.7R, Sharpe 0.83 | 1,355, +176.7R, 0.83 ✓ |
| Noise band NQ (walk-forward) | 859 trades, +52.0R, Sharpe 0.71 | 859, +52.0R, 0.71 (0.70 over 63 months, first month has no trades) ✓ |
| ATR band NQ | 828 trades, +50.7R, Sharpe 1.00 | 828, +50.7R from Jan 2021; 766 / +43.8R inside the Jul 2021–Sep 2026 window; Sharpe 1.00 ✓ |
| Expiry NQ / ES | 65 trades each, +14.1R / +9.0R | 65 / +14.1R, 65 / +9.0R from Jan 2021 (60 each inside the window) ✓ |

## Data bug found and fixed (2026-10-27)
`data/databento/NQ_2026-09.csv.gz` overlaps `NQ_2026-partial.csv.gz` (both hold September 2026). The deep-dive loader read
both, so every September 2026 minute was counted twice (noise band came out 862 trades / +51.5R). Both loaders now keep one

# Batch 43 results: month-end stock-bond rebalancing trade on NQ

Rules: `analysis/BATCH43_PREREG.md` (Claude's own idea, 28 Nov 2026). Code: `analysis/batch43.py`. Data:
`analysis/batch43_lockbox2010.json`, `analysis/batch43_databento.json`. First run, no reruns.

## Verdict: REJECTED

It helped a lot in 2011-2020 and hurt in 2022-2026. The bar needs both eras.

| | 2011-2020 (lockbox2010) | 2022-2026 (databento) |
|---|---|---|
| Book alone: Sharpe / CAGR / worst drop | 0.945 / 19.1% / 23.4% | 1.288 / 42.4% / 20.5% |
| Book + trade: Sharpe / CAGR / worst drop | 1.114 / 25.2% / 24.5% | **1.141** / 38.5% / 24.1% |
| Sharpe gain | +0.169 | **-0.147** |
| Trades / win rate | 114 / 54% | 58 / 50% |
| Avg return per trade after costs (1x notional) | +0.45% | -0.18% |
| Own Sharpe | 0.59 | -0.20 |
| Short side (stocks beat bonds): n / win / avg | 76 / 46% / -0.00% | 35 / 49% / -0.53% |
| Long side (bonds beat stocks): n / win / avg | 38 / 71% / +1.34% | 23 / 52% / +0.36% |
| Correlation with the book | -0.03 | +0.02 |
| Luck check: share of draws with gain <= 0 | 0.09 | 0.92 |

## Plain English
The idea was to trade against month-end pension rebalancing: short Nasdaq in the last five sessions when stocks beat
bonds that month, long when bonds won. In 2011-2020 all of the edge came from the long side (buying after a bad month
for stocks); the short side, the one the rebalancing story is really about, earned nothing. In 2022-2026 the short
side lost and the long side shrank, so the trade cut the book's Sharpe by 0.15. In the first era it was mostly a
"buy the dip near month end" trade, not a rebalancing trade, and that did not carry over.

Trial count after this batch: about 332.

# Batch 42 results: trend sleeve, gold (GC) + 10-year Treasury (ZN), monthly momentum

Rules: `analysis/BATCH42_PREREG.md` (issue #2). Code: `analysis/batch42.py`. Data: `analysis/batch42_lockbox2010.json`,
`analysis/batch42_databento.json`. Run: https://github.com/drusiyani/argon-v2/actions/runs/46133185539 (first run, no reruns).

## Verdict: PASS (weak, could be luck) — for Dru to decide

The full book's Sharpe rose in both eras after costs, so the fixed bar is met. But the luck check is weak: in about a
quarter of the bootstrap draws the gain was zero or less, in both eras. Nothing in the live book has changed.

| | 2011-2020 (lockbox2010) | 2022-2026 (databento) |
|---|---|---|
| Book alone (core + four rules): Sharpe / CAGR / worst drop | 0.945 / 19.1% / 23.4% | 1.288 / 42.4% / 20.5% |
| Book + sleeve: Sharpe / CAGR / worst drop | **1.034** / 22.4% / 23.4% | **1.376** / 47.9% / 19.1% |
| Sharpe gain | +0.089 | +0.088 |
| Sleeve's own Sharpe (GC / ZN alone) | 0.35 (0.14 / 0.39) | 0.51 (0.42 / 0.30) |
| Sleeve volatility a year | 8.6% | 7.9% |
| Correlation with the core / the book | -0.11 / -0.08 | -0.06 / -0.00 |
| Luck check: share of draws with gain <= 0 | 0.27 | 0.25 |
| Luck check: 5th / 50th percentile gain | -0.15 / +0.08 | -0.12 / +0.08 |

- Trades: one rebalance per market per month end, 184 month ends from Jun 2011 to Sep 2026 (each a small resize; the
  side flips far less often). Avg R does not apply: the sleeve is a sized holding, not R-based trades.
- 2022 (the year it was meant for): sleeve +8.5%, book alone -5.1%, book with sleeve +3.6%.
- Sleeve by year: 2011 +13.3, 2012 -1.9, 2013 +12.2, 2014 -1.6, 2015 +7.0, 2016 -9.7, 2017 +0.3, 2018 -8.3,
  2019 +1.9, 2020 +15.2, 2022 +8.5, 2023 -7.3, 2024 +6.3, 2025 +8.6, 2026 +3.3 (to end Oct).
- Info only: whole contracts on $100k (MGC + ZN): book Sharpe 1.074 / 1.399. Roll cost 2 ticks instead of 1:
  1.031 / 1.374. Costs barely matter here (about 12 resizes a year per market).

## Plain English
The sleeve does what it was built for. It is nearly uncorrelated with the Nasdaq core, and it made money in 2022 when
the book lost. Adding it lifted the book's Sharpe by about 0.09 in both eras, with costs, and never made the worst
drop worse. But the sleeve on its own is weak (Sharpe 0.35-0.51) and lumpy: it lost 8-10% in 2016, 2018 and 2023.
A gain of 0.09 is small next to the noise. The bootstrap says roughly a 1 in 4 chance the true gain is zero or
negative in each era. Also, trend in gold and bonds is a well-known, crowded premium, so the 2011-2020 result is the
fairer guide, not a surprise discovery. Small caveats: GC/ZN daily closes are about 4 hours after the Nasdaq close, and
the data ends 30 Oct 2026, so the sleeve is flat for Nov 2026.

Trial count after this batch: about 331.

title: Batch 34 results: is G3 real once every test is counted? (20 Nov 2026)
text:
# Batch 34 results: is G3 real once every test is counted? (20 Nov 2026)

Rules: `BATCH34_PREREG.md` (commit 3d50cad, before the run). Code: `batch34.py`, `batch34_power.py`. Output: `batch34.json`,
`batch34_power.json`. Analysis only; nothing in the race changes until an amendment says so.

## A. Deflated Sharpe (is G3 better than zero after ~299 tries?): FAIL as registered, pass on the fairer reading
| | 2021-26 | 2010-20 |
|---|---|---|
| G3 Sharpe (a year) | 1.76 | 1.41 |
| Luck bar, N = 299, spread of ALL saved trials | 1.45 | 1.15 |
| Deflated Sharpe probability, N = 299 (pass mark 0.95) | **0.79** | **0.81** |
| Same, N = 50 | 0.95 | 0.95 |
| Same, N = 299, spread of package-level trials only | 1.00 | 1.00 |

The registered test fails: the saved trials range from "index alone" (Sharpe ~0.5) to package variants (~1.8), and that
wide spread sets a high luck bar. Counting only the trials G3 was really picked from (package variants), it passes easily.
Honest reading: G3's Sharpe is very unlikely to be pure luck, but the strict version of the test does not prove it.

## B. Is G3's gain over the plain package real? FAIL
| | 2021-26 | 2010-20 | pooled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Extra return a year | +2.0% | +5.7% | +4.4% |
| t (Newey-West) | 0.55 | 2.40 | 2.20 |
| Bootstrap p | 0.29 | 0.007 | 0.013 |

Bars: 3.59 for the best of 299, 3.09 for the best of 50. Pooled t = 2.20 clears neither. In the era G3 was built on,
its gain is indistinguishable from zero. As registered: G3 stays the main book, but the write-up must say its gain over
the package is not proven.

## C. The four rules before and after May 2024 (when the noise-area paper was published), 2021-26 era
| rule | before: trades, mean R, t | from May 2024: trades, mean R, t |
|---|---|---|
| QuantLab | 671, +0.12, 1.44 | 598, **+0.20, 1.79** |
| Noise band | 495, +0.08, 1.63 | 392, +0.05, **0.78** (flagged) |
| ATR band | 486, +0.08, 2.65 | 351, +0.04, 0.95 |
| Expiry | 76, +0.29, 2.45 | 56, +0.11, 0.78 |

Every rule except QuantLab weakened after May 2024. Since then QuantLab made 122R of the four rules' 161R; the other three
are near zero, and for each of them the best 10 days made more than their whole total. Matches NostroBenJ's finding that
the noise-area breakout faded after publication (NQ Sharpe 1.49 -> 0.88, ES 1.78 -> -0.19).

## D. Power of the desk's promotion rule (added after A-C; not pre-registered)
Simulated on G3's rules sleeve. "Skill" = how well the AI's size tracks the day's result (AUC 0.50 = none, 0.54 = small,
0.58 = clear).

| rule | 120 days: no skill / small / clear | 230 days: no skill / small / clear |
|---|---|---|
| Today's rule (Sharpe beats both arms by +0.15) | **23%** / 48% / 66% | **17%** / 49% / 77% |
| Shuffle test (beats 95% of its own sizes reshuffled) | 5% / 25% / 63% | 6% / 37% / 88% |

Today's promotion rule promotes an AI with no skill about one time in five, and finds a small real skill only about
half the time: close to a coin flip. The shuffle test keeps false promotions at 5% and is better at catching clear skill.
Recommendation for the freeze: replace the +0.15 rule with the shuffle test, and say in advance that ~230 days can only
detect a clear skill, not a small one.

## Triage of the rest of T13 (not tested, with reasons)
- Answered a different list of "Ideas 1–10" (60/40 rebalancing, dash-for-cash, COT, VVIX, fixed-share, LETF…), not
  the T13 brief; no ranked odds, no do-nothing assessment, no view on 0.5% vs 0.625%.

  same in points in 2010, so friction really was ~10× larger relative to price. Batch 22 showed this is why the rules
  lost money before 2018. Scaling costs to price would flatter 2010–20 falsely.
- Idea 12 (0DTE hedge unwind): needs OPRA options data, post-2022 only. Cannot pass both eras; at most a live log.
- Idea 14 (30-min noise band + VWAP): already the book's noise-band rule.

  is reported dead by Gemini's own sources; roll week already tested (batch 29).
- Idea 13 (multi-horizon vol overlay): a variant of the core's VXN sizing and H3 (failed batch 9). Low priority.
- Idea 15 (net Fed liquidity, auctions): a monthly 4-month-lagged signal from a non-peer-reviewed post; core-level,
  slow, small sample. Not tested.
- Race 1 scoring advice (rank correlation and AUC rather than binned Brier scores; recalibrate the AIs out of fold;
  leave-two-out P&L): sound and consistent with T12. **Adopt for the desk evaluation.**
- Many 2026 citations (Nov 2026 working papers, CFTC release 9316-26, Databento's $199/month price, arXiv 2608.03703)

title: Batch 30 results: core / rules split under G3 (16 Nov 2026)
Batch 29 results: "the unknown" (15–16 Nov 2026)
text:
# Batch 29 results: "the unknown" (15–16 Nov 2026)

Rules and marks were committed first (`BATCH29_PREREG.md`, plus two addenda, each committed before its checks ran).
Format: return a year / Sortino / worst drop / crash chance. Running total: about 279 trials.

## Headline
1. **No new edge.** Ten unusual ideas plus one follow-up: none is an adopt candidate.
2. **The search found something more useful: how much of G3's headline was luck.** Adding three facts that carry no
   information at all moved G3's return by several points. The honest expectation for G3 is its jitter median:
   **+58.5% / 3.34 / −18.6% (2021–26) and +28.4% / 2.32 / −21.2% (2010–20)**, not +60.2% and +29.1%.
3. **G3 and skip-only cannot be told apart.** Differences under about 3 points (2021–26) or 1.5 points (2010–20)
   are inside the noise of the measurement.

## The ten ideas
| | 2021–26 | 2010–20 | Strict vs G3 | Luck (of 5,000) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G3 (reference, single run) | +60.2% / 3.41 / −18.4% / 0.7% | +29.1% / 2.36 / −21.2% / 0.9% | | | |
| U1 noise band 5 min early (no model, vs package) | +57.6% / 3.18 / −20.6% / 1.8% | +20.3% / 1.69 / −21.9% / 7.8% | no (vs package) | | fail |
| U1 control: 5 min late | +55.7% / 3.17 / −20.5% / 0.9% | +22.4% / 1.80 / −22.6% / 6.4% | no | | |
| U2 sibling labels | +54.3% / 3.14 / −19.7% / 0.9% | +29.2% / 2.36 / −21.2% / 1.4% | no | 2 | fail |
| U3 QuantLab six-variant ensemble | +51.5% / 3.09 / −19.0% / 0.6% | +28.5% / 2.36 / −20.0% / 1.0% | no | | fail |
| U4 signal-candle shape | +60.7% / 3.48 / −18.7% / 0.6% | +29.4% / 2.38 / −21.2% / 0.9% | **yes** | 0 | fails check C (below) |
| U4b shape facts for every rule | +60.0% / 3.40 / −18.8% / 0.7% | +28.5% / 2.34 / −21.5% / 1.3% | no | 0 | fail |
| U5 recency weighting (3-year half-life) | +50.7% / 2.97 / −20.2% / 0.5% | +26.8% / 2.20 / −21.2% / 2.4% | no | 6 | fail |
| U6 longs ×0.75, shorts ×1.25 | +60.3% / 3.41 / −19.7% / 0.3% | +28.0% / 2.27 / −22.2% / 2.1% | no | 2,058 | fail |
| U7 night-heavy core (unlocked) | +57.1% / 3.30 / −17.7% / 0.3% | +21.0% / 1.78 / −26.3% / 7.5% | no | | fail |
| U8 model as a forecast for the core | not unlocked | | | | no rule tested |
| U9 plumbing calendar (5 flags) | none unlocked | | | | no rule tested |
| U10 news-candle trades | +54.6% / 3.12 / −19.8% / 1.3% | +28.3% / 2.29 / −21.2% / 1.2% | no | | fail |

## What each one showed
- **U1, the public clock.** Friction-free noise-band R a year, early / on the clock / late:
  2010–20: 5.0 / 7.4 / 8.7. 2021–May 2024: 14.3 / 12.9 / 13.3. Jun 2024–Nov 2026: **12.6 / 10.4 / 6.7**.
  After the May 2024 paper, being five minutes early beat being five minutes late by about 6R a year; before it there
  was no such gap (in 2010–20 late was better). That is the footprint a crowd on the :00/:30 clock would leave. It is
  2.5 years of data and the package test failed, so it is **logged as a watch item, not adopted**.
- **U2.** Sibling labels are 93% correlated with the trade's own label; almost no noise is removed. Worse in 2021–26.
- **U3.** The monthly pick has real skill in 2021–26 (35.3 vs 20.8 net R a year for the plain six-way average) and none
  in 2010–20 (4.0 vs 4.7). Averaging the six throws that skill away.
- **U4.** Passed the strict mark by half a point. Harder checks: junk-facts twin 0 of 300 (pass); double costs
  +56.0% vs +55.1% and +24.0% vs +23.6% (pass); sub-periods level-or-better in only 3 of 5 (2018–20: 68.1 vs 68.8,
  2021–25: 64.9 vs 66.1; **fail**, needed 4). Only one of the three facts is stable: where the candle closed within
  its range (weight positive in 88% of monthly refits). The trades whose call changed were no better than the ones
  they replaced. **Not adopted.**
- **U5.** Forgetting old trades faster hurt in both eras. The long history is helping, not hurting.
- **U6.** Shorts do hedge the core (daily correlation −0.28 / −0.24 vs +0.27 / +0.19 for longs), but in 2010–20 they
  earned a third of what longs did (+0.03R vs +0.10R), so leaning on them cost return and deepened the worst drop.
- **U7.** The Nasdaq's night leg has the better Sharpe in both eras (0.49 vs 0.33 in 2021–26; 1.20 vs 0.50 in 2010–20).
  Before switching costs a night-heavy core gave +60.2% / 3.44 / −17.6% and +31.1% / 2.52 / −21.2%. Switching twice a
  day costs more than it earns: fails at the pre-registered cost, and at half that cost it still would not beat G3's
  return in 2021–26.
- **U8.** Top-third forecast days were more volatile in both eras, but the Nasdaq's average move on them was lower in
  2021–26 (−4 bp vs +4 bp) and higher in 2010–20 (+4 bp vs 0 bp). No rule unlocked.
- **U9.** Pooled p-values: clock mismatch 0.32, VIX settlement 0.44, quarter end 0.80, after a holiday 0.83,
  **roll week 0.035** (kept trades averaged −0.06R in roll weeks vs +0.22R otherwise, worse in both eras). The bar was
  0.01 for five tests, so nothing unlocked. Roll week is logged as a watch item.
- **U10.** Following the 8:30 news candle loses: −0.13R and −0.11R a trade net, 42% and 38% winners, worse than the
  same rule on ordinary days. No drift to harvest after the first five minutes.

## Jitter test of our own recommendation (addendum 2)
Three pure-noise facts added to the 24, 300 runs each. Median (5%–95% range):

| | Return 2021–26 | Sortino | Worst drop | Return 2010–20 | Sortino | Worst drop |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Package (no model) | +56.4% | 3.18 | −19.4% | +21.6% | 1.75 | −23.5% |
| G3, single run | +60.2% | 3.41 | −18.4% | +29.1% | 2.36 | −21.2% |
| **G3, jitter** | **+58.5%** (53.0 to 61.9) | 3.34 (3.08 to 3.50) | −18.6% | **+28.4%** (26.7 to 29.9) | 2.32 (2.20 to 2.43) | −21.2% |
| Skip-only, single run | +57.9% | 3.30 | −18.8% | +28.5% | 2.29 | −21.2% |
| **Skip-only, jitter** | **+57.8%** (52.9 to 61.6) | 3.30 (3.07 to 3.49) | −18.9% | **+28.8%** (27.7 to 30.0) | 2.32 (2.24 to 2.42) | −21.9% |

- G3 jitter runs beat the package in both eras on return 73% of the time, on Sortino 84%, and had a worst drop no
  deeper than the package 79% of the time. Skip-only: 75%, 84%, 59%.
- With the noise placed on QuantLab trades only (a harsher test): G3 median +56.2% / +26.8%, beating the package on
  return in both eras 48% of the time and on Sortino 65%. Skip-only: +54.6% / +27.5%, 28% and 42%.
- **Why so sensitive:** QuantLab's tight-stop trades have rare very large winners (a +10R trade is about 5% of the
  account at these sizes). Flip a handful of keep/skip calls and the yearly figure moves by points.
- **By the rules fixed in advance:** skip-only does not beat G3 on jitter medians in both eras, so **G3 stays the main
  book**; G3's Sortino improvement is robust (84% ≥ 80%). G3's quoted numbers become the jitter medians.

## What this means
- What the trade-selection model reliably adds over the package: about +2 points of return in 2021–26 and +7 in
  2010–20, a better Sortino, and a slightly shallower worst drop. That is the size of the edge found in 29 batches.
- The strict mark was resolving half-point differences that do not exist. Several earlier near-misses and near-passes
  (batches 24–28) were inside this noise. Future model comparisons should use jitter medians.
- More backtest tweaks will not find a bigger edge with this data: the yardstick is coarser than anything left to
  find. New information has to come from Race 1 itself (the AI desk) and from live paper trades.

## Watch items for the desk log (no rule attached)
1. Published-clock footprint (U1): track early-vs-late noise-band results live.
2. Roll week (U9).
3. Mega-cap pre-earnings freeze (S1, batch 26).

- **Gemini's power estimate used too small a spread.** G3's daily rules R has a standard deviation of 2.03R, not the 1.10R it
  assumed. The correlation the AI desk needs to show (about 0.12 for p < 0.05) does not change, but the profit that

| G3 | +60.2% / 3.41 / −18.4% / 0.7% | +29.1% / 2.36 / −21.2% / 0.9% | — | — |
| G3c recalibrated | +51.1% / 3.00 / −18.7% / 0.7% | +28.9% / 2.33 / −21.2% / 0.9% | no | 0 |

Sub-periods (return a year / worst drop), G3 → G3c: 2010–13 +17.9% → +18.1%; 2014–17 +14.2% → +13.4%; 2018–20 +68.8% →
+69.1%; **2021–25 +66.1% → +54.6%**; 2026 +30.5% → +32.4%.

## Why
Claude's stated expectation ("roughly the same return") was wrong for 2021–26. When the offset went negative, G3c skipped
extra trades that turned out to be among the best: 2021, 49 trades averaging +0.34R; 2023, 35 trades averaging +0.70R;
2024, 3 trades averaging **+10.8R**. These are tight-stop trades whose predicted edge sat just above the friction line. Most
lose a little, but a few become huge winners in R terms. Lowering the predictions pushed them under the line.
In 2026 it did what was intended (3 extra skips averaging −0.82R, +1.9 points), but that is far too small to pay for 2021–25.

## Lesson
G3's friction hurdle should not be made stricter. The overconfidence found in batch 26 is real, but trading on it removes
the rare large winners that the rules depend on. Protection against a fading edge belongs in a separate stop rule, not in G3.
About 261 trials in total.

## Part 2 kill switches, by sub-period (return a year / worst drop)

| | 2010–13 | 2014–17 | 2018–20 | 2021–25 | 2026 | Weight on 13 Nov 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G3, no switch | +17.9% / −21.2% | +14.2% / −19.8% | +68.8% / −18.4% | +66.1% / −17.7% | +30.5% / −18.4% | 1 |

- **K2** is the only one that behaved like insurance: it was at half or zero weight for most of 2014–17 (a weak stretch),

  market prediction". The 2010–20 gain is mostly risk (crash chance 2.4% → 0.9%); return rises only 0.6 points.

# Batch 23 results (14 Nov 2026): by the rule fixed in advance, the model's skill "does not carry"; the detail is mixed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| (a) top minus bottom above zero in 2010–13 AND 2014–17, all test trades | yes (+0.05R, +0.31R) |
| (b) the same for never-seen QuantLab trades | **no** (−0.06R in 2010–13, +0.40R in 2014–17) |
| (c) skip-only beats the scenario package over 2010–17 | yes |
| (d) under 5% of random rules beat skip-only | yes (0.4%) |

(b) failed, and the rule said that if (a) or (b) fails the reading is "does not carry". That stands.

## The detail
Average R per trade in the scenario, bottom third / middle / top third (t-statistic of top minus bottom):

| | 2010–13 | 2014–17 |
|---|---|---|
| All test trades | −0.02 / +0.01 / +0.03 (t 0.5) | −0.06 / +0.12 / +0.25 (t 3.4) |
| Never-seen QuantLab | +0.02 / +0.04 / −0.04 (t −0.3) | −0.13 / +0.31 / +0.27 (t 2.1) |
| Noise band + ATR band | −0.03 / +0.02 / +0.04 (t 1.1) | −0.07 / −0.07 / +0.21 (t 3.4) |

- In 2010–13 there was almost no edge to rank (batch 22: +0R to +26R a year before friction), and the model found nothing.
- In 2014–17, when the edge existed, a model that had only seen 2018–26 separated good from bad trades clearly, including
  on QuantLab trades no scan or model had ever touched.
- The answer does not hinge on the scenario: on friction-free outcomes the gaps are +0.07R (t 0.7) and +0.33R (t 3.6).
- **For QuantLab the model spots the worst trades, not the best.** The top third did no better than the middle third
  (+0.16R against +0.21R over 2010–17). Skipping is supported; pressing is not.

## Package over 2010–17 at today's friction (scenario)
| | Return a year | Sortino | Worst drop | Chance of a drop worse than −35% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed size | +36.1% | 2.62 | −30.4% | 8.9% |
| Skip-only | +42.2% | 3.16 | −22.5% | 3.2% |
| Skip-and-press | +50.2% | 3.38 | −27.3% | 10.3% |
| Core only | +17.8% | 1.66 | −17.1% | 0.0% |

Random rules beating skip-only's return: 21 of 5,000. Beating skip-and-press's: 10 of 5,000.

## What it means
- The model is not a general skill. It works when the momentum edge is there and does nothing when it is not. If 2027 is an
  edge-less year like 2010–13, the model will not rescue the rules; skip-only would still cut exposure by about a third.
- Skip-only is supported again, and with a much shallower worst drop than fixed size in the scenario (−22.5% against −30.4%).
- Skip-and-press is not supported by the unseen QuantLab trades.
- Honest notes from the pre-registration apply: a backward test, scenario outcomes, and the noise band / ATR band trades
  were not clean. This sample is now used and cannot serve as an unseen test again.

Sub-periods (return a year / worst drop): 2010–17 real +10.6% / −23.5%, scenario +36.1% / −30.4%, core only +17.8% / −17.1%.
2018–20 real +53.9% / −20.4%, scenario +85.7% / −20.0%. 2021–25 real +64.2%, scenario +72.0%. 2026 real +19.1%, scenario +19.2%.

Rules' R by year in the scenario: 2010 +4, 2011 −17, 2012 +12, 2013 +7, 2014 +39, 2015 +74, 2016 +36, 2017 +78, 2018 +118,
2019 +88, 2020 +28, 2021 (half) +42, 2022 +78, 2023 +79, 2024 +90, 2025 +56, 2026 +16.

## What this changes
1. **The edge is about 13 years old, not 9**, and it showed up in calm years (2014–17) as well as wild ones. That is better
   evidence that it is a lasting feature of the Nasdaq.
2. **Why "every filter splits the decades":** in the high-friction years the average trade lost money, so anything that
   removed trades helped. In the low-friction years the average trade made money, so removing trades hurt. Many "split"
   verdicts in batches 4–12 were about friction, not about the idea.
3. **"Fitted to the Nasdaq" was too strong.** The same rules have an edge on the S&P before friction. The Nasdaq future is
   simply the one where the tick is small against the index's price and movement.
4. **2026 is still a real worry.** At today's friction it is the weakest full year since 2013 (+16R), in the same range as
   the early years when the edge was close to absent (−17R to +12R).
5. **Risk reads worse, not better.** At today's index level the cost rule no longer keeps QuantLab out in a year with no
   edge. In the scenario the worst drop is −30.4% (2010–17), against −23.5% in real history.
6. The council (14 Nov) was given the withdrawn claim as a fact. Its "nine winning years after eight with nothing" reading
   should be discounted accordingly; its points on costs, tails and 2026 stand.

## Limits
The scenario is hypothetical. When friction was high, nobody could trade this edge away; at today's friction anyone can, so
the scenario probably overstates what the early years would really have paid. It is not used to pass a mark or to argue
for more size.

| Days traded / share of winning days | 1,390 / 52.5% | 2,492 / 50.2% |

## Mark 2 — in the package at 0.5×: FAIL (strict mark)
Each cell: return a year / Sortino / worst drop / bootstrap chance of a drop worse than −35%.

| | 2021–26 | 2010–20 | Strict | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Package | +56.4% / 3.18 / −19.4% / 1.0% | +21.6% / 1.75 / −23.5% / 7.4% | — | — |
| Package + leg | +63.8% / 3.26 / −20.8% / 0.7% | +26.7% / 1.96 / −25.1% / 10.2% | no | no |
| Skip-only | +57.9% / 3.30 / −18.8% / 0.8% | +28.5% / 2.29 / −21.2% / 2.4% | — | — |
| Skip-only + leg | +65.4% / 3.34 / −24.3% / 2.8% | +33.9% / 2.51 / −20.9% / 2.4% | no (2021–26 drop 5.5 points deeper) | no |

It adds return in both eras but also deepens the drops, so it is more exposure, not a free improvement. Not adopted.

## Why it should not be trusted much
- **Three years carry it.** Average return per day (t-statistic): 2010–17 +1.3 bps (0.7); 2018–20 +10.3 (2.5);
  2021–25 +2.4 (0.7); 2026 +18.4 (3.0). By year only 2018, 2020 and 2026 are large; most years are near zero.
- **It fails on the S&P.** 2010–17 −3.0 bps a day (t −2.0), 2018–20 +3.2, 2021–26 +0.5. Not positive in all three periods.
- **It is the same bet as the rules.** Correlation with the rules' daily result is 0.33–0.38.
- Batch 20's lesson applies: one narrow pass after about 230 tries is weak evidence.

## What it settles about the "shaken out" idea
On days the stopped QuantLab trade lost, the hold leg lost too: −13.9 bps a day in 2021–26 (t −3.8), −6.9 in 2010–20.
On days it won, the leg made +51 and +59 bps. So when the stop is hit, the direction was usually wrong for the rest of the
day as well. Claude's 14 Nov explanation of 2026 ("right direction, stopped out first") was wrong, which is also why the
second-chance re-entry (batch 18) lost.

## QuantLab before the cost rule (diagnostic)
Picked trades on all signal days, R before costs / after costs / share the cost rule removed:
2011 −70 / −121 / 80%; 2012 −64 / −121 / 91%; 2013 −44 / −106 / 97%; 2014 −22 / −67 / 90%; 2015 +11 / −26 / 89%;
2016 +13 / −27 / 89%; 2017 −3 / −42 / 87%; 2018 +26 / +6 / 28%; 2019 +88 / +66 / 39%; 2020 +4 / −7 / 5%;

QuantLab's result before costs rose from clearly negative (2011–14) to a peak in 2024 and has fallen by about half in each
year since. The cost rule kept it almost entirely out of the book before 2018.

# Batch 20 results (14 Nov 2026): how real are the findings?

Pre-registration: `BATCH20_PREREG.md` (committed before the run). Code: `batch20.py`. Raw: `batch20.json`. No new strategy.

## Part 1 — Search-luck test: "unlikely to be search luck" for both, but passing a mark alone means little
20,000 random rules each (the model's own sizes shuffled among each year's trades).

| | Skip-only | Skip-and-press |
|---|---|---|
| Model's return a year (2021–26 / 2010–20) | +57.9% / +28.5% | +72.9% / +31.5% |
| Average random rule | +47.7% / +21.3% | +55.0% / +21.8% |
| Random rules beating the model's return in BOTH eras | 1 of 20,000 | 0 of 20,000 |
| Chance the best of 230 random rules beats it in both eras | 1.1% (upper bound 3.4%) | under 3.4% |
| Random rules that PASS the same mark the model passed (no bootstrap part) | 233 of 20,000 (1.2%) | 1,601 of 20,000 (8.0%) |
| Chance at least one of 230 random rules passes that mark | 93% | 100% |

By the reading fixed in advance (under 5%), both are **unlikely to be search luck**: the two-era requirement is what does
the work, since a random rule beat skip-only in 2021–26 alone 445 times in 20,000.
The second finding matters as much: **passing a mark is weak evidence**. After about 230 tries, something would almost
certainly have passed the strict or growth mark by luck. What is rare is the size of the model's lead. The hand rules from
batches 11–12 (which only just passed, or just failed) deserve less weight than the model for this reason.
Limits: random shuffles are not the ~230 ideas actually tried, and this does not measure the hindsight in the feature list.

## Part 2 — Correction: QuantLab's direction in 2026 was right 58.6% of the time, not 65%
The 65% used the day's open-to-close move, which includes the candle that makes the signal. From the entry price to the close:

| Year | Old figure | From entry | Held to the close with no stop, avg R | Actual avg R (before costs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 58% | 53% | +1.40 | +0.07 |
| 2019 | 55% | 46% | +0.01 | +0.32 |
| 2020 | 60% | 53% | +0.80 | +0.09 |
| 2021 | 51% | 46% | −0.81 | +0.21 |
| 2022 | 61% | 55% | +0.34 | +0.14 |
| 2023 | 56% | 51% | −0.13 | +0.19 |
| 2024 | 58% | 50% | +0.11 | +0.35 |
| 2025 | 63% | 58% | +0.42 | +0.17 |
| 2026 | 65% | **59%** | **+1.41** | +0.08 |

2026 is still QuantLab's best year for direction, so the "right direction, stopped out first" reading survives, at a smaller
size. The no-stop column is in each trade's own R (a tight stop, so these positions would be far too big to hold without one);
it shows that in 2018 and 2026 the direction kept paying after the stop was hit, while in 2021 and 2023 the stop saved money.

## Part 3 — Costs in R terms, and a finding about the "sealed decade"
Average cost per momentum trade: 0.044–0.049R in 2010–13, 0.036–0.041R in 2015–19, 0.024R in 2020, 0.013–0.022R in 2021–25,
**0.010R in 2026**. The same 0.75 points costs about a quarter of what it did in 2011–14, because the index is ten times higher.

This exposed something not noticed before. QuantLab trades in the book per year: 2011 48, 2012 22, 2013 7, 2014 23, 2015 25,
2016 26, 2017 32, then 2018 170, 2019 148, 2020 228, and 121–238 a year since. QuantLab signals almost every day (about 240
a year), so **the cost rule removed 80–97% of QuantLab's trades before 2018**. Consequences:
- The 2010–17 results are mostly the noise band and ATR band. They say little about QuantLab, which is now the main engine
  (17.7 of the rules' 29.8 points a year in 2021–26).
- The "break in 2018" is partly the cost rule switching QuantLab on as the index and volatility rose, not only a change in
  the market. (Lockbox 2 did show QuantLab had no edge before costs over 2011–20 as a whole, so both things are true.)
- 2013–17 is not a clean picture of "what if the edge disappears in 2027": at today's index level the cost rule would not
  switch QuantLab off.

| G2 gamma reallocation | +45.3% / 2.61 / −25.2% / 3.7% | +27.6% / 2.06 / −25.5% / 12.1% | no | no |

## Q — the second chance loses everywhere, worst of all in 2026
Re-entry trades (all six variants, before the monthly re-pick), average R after costs:
2010–17 −0.26 (2,813 trades), 2018–20 −0.21 (982), 2021–25 −0.01 (1,798), **2026 −0.25 (376)**.
When QuantLab is shaken out early, the second attempt usually gets shaken out too. Being "right on the direction" by the
close does not help when the path keeps whipping. Hypothesis rejected.

## G — dealer gamma: the effect reverses between eras
Rules' average R per day, by SqueezeMetrics GEX regime (yesterday's GEX vs its one-year median):

| | Low gamma | High gamma |
|---|---|---|
| 2011–17 | −0.02 (656 days) | −0.07 (875) |
| 2018–20 | **+0.39** (368) | −0.07 (380) |
| 2021–26 | +0.11 (662) | **+0.31** (785) |

In 2011–20 the theory held: the rules did better when dealers were less long gamma. In 2021–26 it reversed: the rules did
better on HIGH-gamma days. So the published "long gamma kills momentum" story, as measured by this S&P-based number, does not
explain Argon's 2021–26 results. Possible reasons: GEX is an S&P measure, not Nasdaq; SqueezeMetrics' method may have
changed; or same-day options changed what the end-of-day number means after about 2022. None of these is tested here.

## What this batch says
Neither fix for 2026's whipsaw works. The whipsaw looks like something to survive (smaller size, skip-only, a stop rule),
not something to trade around. About 223 trials in total.

# Batch 15 results (14 Nov 2026): why, what if we're wrong, and how much to bet

Pre-registration: `BATCH15_PREREG.md` (committed before the run). Code: `batch15_index.py`, `batch15.py`. Raw: `batch15.json`.

## Part A — Mechanism on the index itself (no rules involved)

**1. "A trend day is followed by a sideways day": NOT supported.** After the top fifth of days by move size, the next day's
move was bigger, not smaller, in every period and in both markets (Nasdaq: 0.51 vs 0.45, 0.56 vs 0.46, 0.50 vs 0.48 ATR).
Straightness the next day was about the same (higher in 2010–17, a little lower in 2018–20 and 2021–26). So the reason
Claude gave in batches 11–12 for the "day after a win is bad" pattern was wrong, and that pattern currently has no
explanation. A pattern with no explanation deserves less trust.

**2. "The day follows the overnight gap": true only when the gap goes against yesterday, and fading.**
Average open→close return in the gap's direction, basis points a day (t-statistic):

| | 2010–17 | 2018–20 | 2021–26 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nasdaq, gap against yesterday | +5.8 (2.1) | +15.7 (2.4) | +1.7 (0.4) |
