The effect is real in 2010–20 in both markets, which supports the gap pattern. In 2021–26 it has almost gone on the Nasdaq
and gone on the S&P.

## Part B — Gap-continuation trade: FAIL (alone)
Condition met (positive in all three periods), so it was run. Alone at 1×: 2010–20 +6.7% a year, Sharpe 0.67;
2021–26 +3.6% a year, Sharpe 0.29 (needs 0.30). Not added to the package.

## Part C — Betting more on the model-sized rules: stays at 0.5
Each cell: return a year / Sharpe / worst drop / bootstrap chance of a drop worse than −35%.

| Rules weight | 2021–26 | 2010–20 | Growth mark |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 (candidate) | +72.3% / 1.73 / −22.5% / 1.2% | +28.1% / 1.21 / −23.5% / 6.2% | yes |

| 1.0 | +132.3% / 1.68 / −37.5% / 58.5% | +32.2% / 0.93 / −32.9% / 86.0% | no |

In 2010–20, doubling the rules' weight adds 4 points of return and takes the crash chance from 6% to 86%. Sharpe falls in
both eras as the weight rises. More weight is more risk, not more skill.

## Part D — What if we are wrong? (return a year / worst drop)

| | 2013–17 (rules had no edge) | 2018–20 | 2021–25 | 2026 so far |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core only, no rules | +17.4% / −17.1% | +28.2% / −17.8% | +20.4% / −25.8% | +10.0% / −14.1% |
| Package today | +9.5% / −23.5% | +53.9% / −20.4% | +64.2% / −19.4% | +19.1% / −18.9% |
| Model-sized, rules 0.5 | +11.9% / −23.5% | +75.1% / −21.6% | +80.8% / −17.4% | +31.4% / −22.5% |

When the rules have no edge they cost the package about 8 points a year against holding the core alone, with a deeper drop.
Model sizing cuts that cost to about 5.5 points. When the edge is there, the rules add 25 to 60 points a year.
So the rules are a bet with a known price: roughly 6 to 8 points a year if the edge is gone, for as long as they stay switched on.

Pre-registration: `BATCH11_PREREG.md` (committed before the package test). Code: `batch11.py`. Raw: `batch11_*.json`.

## Part 1 — Attribution (diagnostics, no pass mark)

**Where the package's return comes from (arithmetic % a year, rules at half size)**

| Piece | 2021–26 | 2010–20 |
|---|---|---|
| VXN-managed Nasdaq core | 12.3 | 18.4 |
| Pre-FOMC tilt | 3.9 | 1.1 |
| T-bill interest | 3.3 | 0.6 |
| QuantLab | 17.7 | 2.0 |
| Noise band | 5.0 | −0.2 |
| ATR band | 4.7 | −0.9 |
| Expiry reversal | 2.4 | 0.8 |
| (costs inside the rule lines) | −4.3 | −7.2 |

**The rules are a "lose a little most days, win big on wild days" bet.** On the Nasdaq's worst 5% of days they made +2.0% a
day (2021–26) and +1.2% (2010–20); on its best 5% of days +1.2% and +0.7%; on the ordinary 90% of days they lost 0.04% and
0.10% a day.

**The break is 2018, not 2021.** The three momentum rules, R before / after costs, by year:
2010 −8/−11, 2011 −4/−20, 2012 +8/−5, 2013 −9/−21, 2014 −4/−17, 2015 +3/−7, 2016 −4/−17, 2017 +12/−1,
2018 +78/+61, 2019 +35/+19, 2020 +49/+37, 2021 +40/+33, 2022 +65/+57, 2023 +79/+68, 2024 +97/+89, 2025 +60/+53, 2026 +20/+16 (to 12 Nov).
Eight years with no edge even before costs, then nine winning years in a row, five of which (2018–20, 2025–26) were never
used to pick the rules. Volatility does not explain the break: 2015, 2016 and 2019 had the same average daily range
(1.4% of price) and only 2019 made money. That is why every volatility or day-type filter "splits the decades".

**The edge is shrinking.** After costs: 2024 +89R, 2025 +53R, 2026 +16R so far, and −5R since July 2026. Two of the five
deepest package drops in 2021–26 were caused mostly by the rules, both in the last 12 months
(Nov 2025–Jan 2026 and July 2026).

**Drops:** the two deepest in 2021–26 (both 2022) came from the core. In 2010–20 they were shared between core and rules.

## Part 2 — Overnight-gap direction (found by looking; see the pre-registration)

**Lesson:** fading the Nasdaq during the day lost money even in calm markets. Add this to the overnight-reversal fail. The book's
edge is intraday momentum, and the opposite side of that trade doesn't pay.

only: the package at 1.25× still has a 21% (2021–26) and 42% (2010–20) chance of a drop worse than −35%.
